maria: Heads up — noticed a spike in client reconnects for SSE on proxy v2 after a ~100s keepalive. Clients seem to fail resume and fully reconnect, causing replay/billing duplicates. timeline ~= 08:14 UTC
sam: hmm can you paste a short log sample and client id?
maria: client=usr-392
maria: log snippet: ```WARN sse: resume-window expired (last-ack=1745128000) proxy=502 on reconnect```
kevin: is this after the ws->sse fallback rollout last night? :thinking:
anya: telemetry shows ~3x reconnect rate on shard us-east-1-a starting 08:13, error=false->resume_reject
maria: console traces also show a route-flip followed by resume token mismatch. snapshot: ```{"route":"us-east-1-a","resume_id":"r-abc","proxy_eid":502}```
oliver: sounds like a race: route swap kills connection before server persisted ack, client resumes -> server rejects -> client falls back and replays. double-charge risk
sam: can we reproduce locally with a proxy TTL tweak? steps?
maria: repro script (quick): ```while true; do curl -i -N 'https://api.redwood.ai/sse?token=REPRO' ; sleep 1; done``` then set proxy idle_ttl=90s and trigger route-swap
kevin: console UX q: should we classify resume-token-mismatch differently? right now it shows as generic stream_error and is noisy
anya: yes. Recommend adding classification 'resume_id_mismatch' and a dashboard panel showing affected routes + last-proxy-event so oncall can correlate with rollouts
maria: ops question: if resume fails, should fallback prefer direct-host route instead of a full reconnect? that reduces replay but might hide root cause in rollout traces
sam: I prefer a short-term guard: if resume_reject && recent_proxy_reset then throttle client-side retries (exponential backoff cap 10s) and emit console suggestion to ops :thumbsup:
